countries.fatf_baseline_snippet: Argentina is a FATF member and GAFILAT member. Its AML/CTF framework is expected to align with FATF Recommendations, notably R.10 (Customer Due Diligence), R.20 (Reporting of Suspicious Transactions), and R.16 (Wire Transfers). Argentina has been subject to FATF mutual evaluation and should consult the FATF country page for the latest evaluation status.

Brazil is a FATF member. Its AML/CTF regime is anchored by the Financial Activities Control Council (COAF) and the Central Bank of Brazil (Bacen). FATF Recommendations R.10 (CDD), R.20 (STR), and R.16 (wire transfers) set the international baseline applicable to all Brazilian reporting entities. Check the FATF country page for the latest mutual evaluation report.

Uruguay is a GAFILAT member (FATF-Style Regional Body for Latin America). While not a direct FATF member, its AML/CTF framework is assessed against FATF standards. R.10 (CDD), R.20 (STR), and R.16 (wire transfers) are the applicable baseline recommendations. Consult the FATF/GAFILAT country page for the latest mutual evaluation.

Aruba is a constituent country of the Kingdom of the Netherlands and is subject to CFATF (Caribbean FATF) mutual evaluations. FATF Recommendations R.10 (CDD), R.20 (STR), and R.16 (wire transfers) form the international baseline. Consult the FATF/CFATF country page for the latest evaluation.

The Bahamas is a CFATF member. Its AML/CTF regime is assessed against FATF standards. FATF Recommendations R.10 (CDD), R.20 (STR), and R.16 (wire transfers) apply to all reporting entities. Consult the CFATF country page for the latest mutual evaluation results.

Barbados is a CFATF member and its AML/CTF framework is assessed against FATF standards. R.10 (CDD), R.20 (STR), and R.16 (wire transfers) are the international baseline recommendations applicable to Barbadian reporting entities. Check the CFATF country page for latest mutual evaluation findings.

countries.fatf_baseline_snippet: The UAE is a FATF member. The UAE was removed from the FATF Grey List in February 2024. Its AML/CTF/PF regime is governed by Federal Decree-Law No. 10 of 2025 (effective 14 October 2025), which replaced Federal Decree-Law No. 20 of 2018. For crypto/VASP queries: CBUAE covers the federal framework; VARA governs Dubai mainland VASPs (Travel Rule threshold: AED 3,500); ADGM/FSRA governs Abu Dhabi free zone; DFSA governs DIFC. R.10 (CDD), R.20 (STR), R.15 (new technologies/VASPs), and R.16 (wire transfers/Travel Rule) are the key applicable recommendations.

countries.fatf_baseline_snippet: Australia is a founding FATF member. Its AML/CTF regime is supervised by AUSTRAC under the AML/CTF Act 2006. FATF Recommendations R.10 (CDD), R.20 (Suspicious Transaction Reporting), and R.16 (Wire Transfers) form the international baseline applicable to all Australian reporting entities. The 2024 Amendment Act (Tranche 2) expands coverage to legal, accounting, real estate and precious-metals sectors from 1 July 2026. The latest mutual evaluation (2015) and upcoming evaluation (onsite November 2026) are available on the FATF country page.

countries.fatf_baseline_snippet: New Zealand is a FATF member (since 1991) and was placed in enhanced follow-up following its April 2021 mutual evaluation (8 Compliant, 21 Largely Compliant, 11 Partially Compliant). New Zealand is transitioning to a single AML/CFT supervisor (Department of Internal Affairs) from July 2026. Consult the FATF country page for the latest mutual evaluation and follow-up progress.
